definition: A browser mode that prevents storing browsing history, cookies, and temporary files locally, but doesn't hide activity from websites, ISPs, or network administrators.
metaDescription: Learn about private browsing mode - what it does and doesn't protect, plus why it matters for your digital privacy and security online.
simpleExplanation: Private browsing is like using a temporary, anonymous session in your web browser. When you close the window, it erases traces of what you visited from your device, but websites and your internet provider can still see your activity.
whyItMatters: Private browsing helps prevent others using your device from seeing your browsing history and keeps websites from accessing stored cookies from previous sessions, providing basic local privacy protection.
technicalDetail: Private browsing creates an isolated session that doesn't write browsing data to persistent storage. It disables history logging, cookie persistence, and form data saving, but doesn't encrypt traffic or hide IP addresses from external observers.

examples.explanation: Using private browsing when buying surprise gifts prevents the items from appearing in your browser history or affecting future targeted ads that your family might see.
Opening private browsing on a library or work computer ensures your login sessions and visited sites aren't saved for the next user to discover.
Private browsing prevents embarrassing or sensitive searches from showing up in your browser's autocomplete suggestions or history when others use your device.
